nrIncident.message:
All lines have reopened between Brighton / Hove and Haywards Heath following an earlier incident where a person was hit by a train. Trains may still be cancelled, delayed by up to 45 minutes or revised.
Disruption is expected until 04:15.
If you've been affected by what happened on the network today, there is always someone to talk to. You can contact the Samaritans on 116 123 from any phone for a confidential chat.
Customer advice:
You can now use your normal route to reach your destination, however services are subject to delays and last minute alterations or cancellations. Whilst trains return to schedule please allow at least an extra 45 minutes to complete your journey.
Please check customer information boards and check online journey planners for the latest travel information.
Ticket acceptance on alternative routes:
To help with your journey you can use the following services at no extra cost to your ticket:
• Alternative Southern services between Brighton and London Victoria
• Alternative Southern services between Barnham and Brighton
• Thameslink services between Brighton and London
• Gatwick Express services between Brighton and London Victoria
• Metrobus route 272 between Brighton, Preston Park, Hassocks, Burgess Hill, Wivelsfield, Haywards Heath, Three Bridges, Crawley
Planning your journey:
For help planning your journey, check live departure boards, view a live network map or see alternative route guides.
If you’re travelling within London, you can use the TfL Journey Planner.
Can you tell me more?
Sadly, a person has been hit by a train on this part of the network. Network Rail and the emergency services are responding to the incident and working to manage the situation as sensitively, quickly and safely as possible.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.
